name: Linear MCP
summary: External Linear connector capability for reading tickets, updating approved execution state, and recording delivery handoffs.

source.sourceName: Linear MCP or Linear plugin connector
source.notes: Connector entry for Linear operations. Linear remains the execution-state source of truth.

useWhen: A ticket must be read, moved through approved states, linked to a branch/PR, or updated with delivery handoff.
A follow-up ticket is explicitly approved or required by repository policy and concrete scope exists.
doNotUseWhen: Creating Linear projects or tickets lacks explicit approval.
The content would expose secrets, customer data, private evidence, or unsupported claims.
routing.fallback: Record local handoff in the PR or repository and update Linear when connector access returns.

inputs.name: linearIssueId
inputs.description: Linear issue identifier and approved action.

outputs.name: linearExecutionState
outputs.description: Updated status, attachments, comments, or follow-up links.

schemas.notes: Delivery comments should follow the repository handoff template.

allowedOperations: Attach approved branch and PR links

cost.costDriver: Linear workspace usage only unless paid changes are introduced.

risks.description: Linear state changes can misrepresent execution or priority.
risks.mitigation: Use only within assigned ticket scope and preserve branch, PR, validation, review, and merge evidence.

governance.dataBoundary: Do not store secrets, customer data, production data, or private evidence in Linear comments.
governance.sensitiveActionBoundary: Do not use Linear status updates to bypass PR review, approval gates, or evidence requirements.
governance.loggingRequirement: Record branch, PR, validations, review findings, merge status, follow-ups, and residual risk.
governance.updatePolicy: Update when Linear workflow states, labels, or connector permissions change.

review.reviewNotes: Pilot connector entry with approval-gated creation and mutation.

examples.scenario: A PR has merged and the ticket needs delivery update.
examples.expectedUse: Update the assigned ticket with branch, PR, merge commit, validations, findings, and residual risk.
examples.expectedNonUse: Do not create unrelated tickets or projects unless explicitly approved.
